answer.rationale: The competitive price cut is triggering churn conversations in price-sensitive SMB segments. However, memory_73 explicitly warns that promotional pricing produces strong short-term acquisition but fails at renewal—exactly the opposite of the primary objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue). Deploying promotional pricing now would compound that known failure mode under pressure. Instead, memory_44 establishes that enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows with higher pipeline quality. The current moment presents an opportunity: while competitors commoditize SMB pricing, we can redirect sales resources toward enterprise accounts where our demo-request and sales-assisted channels outperform. This preserves margin, aligns with proven conversion mechanics, and targets a segment where price competition is weaker. Referral incentives (memory_57) are valuable but address existing customers; activation messaging (memory_91) and onboarding simplification (memory_86) optimize funnel friction but do not directly counter competitive churn. Enterprise sales assist is the only candidate that (1) avoids the known renewal-failure trap of discounting, (2) leverages a proven high-quality conversion path, and (3) shifts competitive dynamics away from price. A standard experiment scaling this reallocation tests whether enterprise pipeline can absorb redirected resources while SMB churn is monitored without a discount response.
